title: The Restocking Fee Kept Back from a Northbeam Returns and Restocking Exchange Difference
content:
The restocking fee still standing on the return is kept back last. Where a restocking fee stands charged against the return and relief against it stands recorded, what is left after that relief is kept back. Where a restocking fee stands charged against the return and no relief against it stands recorded, the whole fee charged is kept back. In any other case nothing is kept back.

## What is read on the return

Two figures standing on the Northbeam Returns and Restocking return are read: the restocking fee charged against it, and the relief recorded against that fee.

| Restocking fee charged against the return | Relief recorded against it | What is kept back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| more than nothing | more than nothing | the fee charged less the relief recorded, rounded to the cent |
| more than nothing | none recorded | the whole fee charged |
| nothing at all | either way | nothing |

## Cases on hypothetical inputs

*A return carrying a restocking fee of 60.00 USD charged against it and relief of 18.00 USD recorded against that fee.* What is left after the relief is 42.00 USD, and 42.00 USD is kept back.

*A return carrying a restocking fee of 60.00 USD charged against it and no relief recorded.* The whole 60.00 USD is kept back.

*A return carrying two fee entries, of 40.00 USD and 20.00 USD, and one relief of 25.00 USD.* The fee charged against the return comes to 60.00 USD and the relief to 25.00 USD, so 35.00 USD is kept back; the figures are read together rather than entry by entry.

*A return with no restocking fee charged against it at all.* Nothing is kept back.
